rv.q: Beneath the Britney Spears, camping minutiae, nervous jokes, and awkward romantic maneuvering is a deeply big-hearted meditation on connection.

Lean-To has wonderful scenes and exchanges but at certain points, the characters tend to ramble on in a way that might feel natural outside of a theater but comes across as rather talky onstage. It is then up to director Jesse Jou and the cast to keep the audience engaged, and fortunately for us, they do this extremely well.
If you're not really, really into camping, Lean-To may feel like a very long hike.

cn.t: Stephen Sheffer's "Lean-To" earns praise as a warm, funny, and unexpectedly poignant exploration of three hikers on a nature trail, with critics highlighting moments of emotional electricity and the play's restorative examination of human connection.
